_comment: spa_routes = SPA-owned page routes. Despite the name, is_spa_route (scripts/gen_routes.py) matches EXACT-OR-SUBTREE for every entry EXCEPT '/': '/calls' owns '/calls/1' and '/b' owns '/b/<slug>' the same way, via `path == r or path.startswith(r.rstrip('/') + '/')`. '/' is special-cased to own ONLY '/' itself, never a subtree -- the general expression above collapses to match EVERY path the moment r.rstrip('/') is the empty string (so startswith('/') is always true), which is exactly the bug the root special-case exists to prevent (is_spa_route's own docstring, gen_routes.py:75-91). HISTORY, so this is not "corrected" a third time: this sentence originally claimed EXACT matching (wrong -- /calls/1 relies on the subtree), was then rewritten without the '/' carve-out (wrong the other way -- it read as matching every path), and is accurate as it now stands. gen_routes.py remains the authority; verify against it before editing this line. /login, /register and the three /auth/* holding pages are React (auth slice). Bare /auth is NOT an spa_route: it would make is_spa_route('/auth/google/start') True and let the dev Vite proxy shadow the real OAuth endpoints (dev-proxy.ts keys off isSpaRoute with no backend-precedence check); the three explicit leaves avoid that. /auth stays in backend_prefixes (doc-only) because POST /auth/google/start + GET /auth/google/callback live there. backend_prefixes / is_backend_route are NOT consulted by the serving or proxy path.
